content.thinking:
I need to write this whole module carefully in one pass since I can't test it, so I'll stick to APIs I'm confident about. I'm designing a hunched swamp troll, about 2.6m tall with a chunky Warcraft-style build, using a green-teal skin palette with moss, a loincloth, bone tusks, and a rusty club, and setting up imports for the builder, paint helpers, texture, and rng utilities.

I'm working out how the builder functions behave -- rods, capsules, spikes, parts, lathes, extrudes, and loft stations with their various positioning options -- plus thinking through a custom paint approach mixing mottled noise with warm top lighting for a hand-painted toon feel. Now I'm blocking out coordinates: the hunched pose with pelvis, torso, and head positions, then working out the leg geometry from hips through knees to ankles and feet, keeping the overall height at 2.5m.

I'm now building out the torso as a series of loft stations from pelvis through belly, chest, to neck base, each with its own width and height, then sweeping a color across it. From there I'm placing shoulder spheres and building the arms as tapered capsules from shoulder to elbow to wrist, ending in fist-shaped hands low enough to nearly touch the ground, with the left hand gripping a club that extends down toward the floor.

I'm positioning the club so its handle rests vertically with a flat cap touching the ground and a heavy spiked frustum head near the top, adjusting the grip point so the troll's fist wraps around the handle naturally. Then I'm placing the head as a skull sphere scaled slightly to give it an elongated, asymmetric shape.

Now I'm sculpting facial features: a brow ridge, an underbite jaw with upward tusks, a bulbous nose with nostrils, glowing yellow eyes with black pupils, and spiky asymmetric ears extending outward from the sides of the skull.

I'm adding a dark green mossy mohawk of spikes running along the back of the head, a spine of hump and spikes down the back, and plotting manual positions for warts scattered across the torso.

For texture I'll scatter small wart spheres across the torso surface and moss patches on the shoulders filtered by upward-facing normals, using flattened spheres or cones instead of cards. Then I'll build a loincloth as a flat hide panel extruded and hung from the hip belt.

Still shaping the loincloth panels...

Adjusting the belt proportions for better overlap, then adding a bronze skull-shaped buckle with hanging bone trinkets at the front. For the shoulder, I'm planning a big spiked leather pauldron using a scaled dome sphere with rivets and bone spikes on the left side.

Now I'm figuring out a bandolier strap draping diagonally across the chest from shoulder to hip, using a surface-drape function to get it to follow the torso's contour before sweeping it into a tube shape, then adding small cone-shaped teeth or bone spikes along its length pointing outward.

I'm also adding fists with claw spikes, toe capsules with claws, and working out a paint function for toad-like skin: a mottled green base texture, lighter yellowish tones on top, darker teal below, and a pale countershaded belly patch defined by normal direction and vertical position.

Now I'm layering in shading logic—blending the base mottled color with darker tones on undersides and lighter highlights on top-facing surfaces, plus muddying the color near the feet.

For the mouth, I'm placing a dark cavity shape under the jaw to suggest an open mouth, with pink gum-colored capsules forming an underbite where the lower jaw protrudes past the upper lip. I also need to double-check I'm not leaving unused imports like noise if I end up skipping the wart detail.

Now I'm building out the skull structure: a main head sphere, a smaller snout sphere pushed forward for the face, and a brow ridge capsule stretching across the top. I'm positioning the eyes just beneath the brow line, nestled into the skull front, with small glowing spheres for the eyes and angled brow rods framing them above.

Working out neck capsule placement and starting the torso loft stations next, with spine spikes to follow for the hunched troll silhouette.

Still working out spike positions and sizes along the back, tapering them down the spine. For the arms, I'll mirror geometry across both sides, giving the right arm a club while the left hangs with a fist hand.

I'm simplifying accessories to a belt pouch instead of a dangling fish, and adding wrist cuffs and forearm bracers as short tapered cylinders positioned using interpolation between elbow and wrist points.

Now I'm shaping the legs with tapered capsules for thighs and shins, spherical feet, and three clawed toes extending from each foot, calculating specific coordinates so everything aligns with the ground plane.

Next I'm planning mossy surface details scattered on the shoulders and hump using a normal-based filter, and designing small mushrooms with cylindrical stalks and spherical caps to stick onto those surfaces.

I'm planning decal details for warpaint and tattoo markings, placing an SVG texture on the chest and skull using surface hit points to position them accurately, with red stripes and bone-white tones.

For the loincloth, I'm defining a paint function that colors a panel based on vertical position, creating stripes and trim patterns along its outline, with a belt region distinguished near the top.

Now I'm shifting to the club: painting a wood-grain texture, then adding a ring of iron nail spikes around the head at various angles and heights, and tilting the handle slightly forward from bottom to top so I can work out where the fist grips it.

Still writing spike geometry math...

Now I'm setting up the color palette for the creature: moss greens for skin, belly tones, warts, leather browns, and bone whites.

I'm checking helper functions like sweep with radius and color options, closed catmull-rom paths, and loft stations for building the mesh geometry.

I'm figuring out spike dimensions and sides options for cheap faceted sweeps, then working out tooth placement as small upward spikes along the jaw capsule's top edge.

For the underbite jaw, I'm positioning the lower jaw capsule to protrude forward with tusk-like spikes angled up and out near the mouth corners, keeping the geometry hidden enough to read as a big troll jaw without exposing gum detail. I'm also adding a thin dark slit box to suggest the closed mouth line.

Now I'm sketching the lip crease as a rod along the jaw front, plus a row of small bone-colored spike teeth jutting up from the lower jaw. For the face, I'm placing a small darker-skin-toned nose sphere with two tiny nostril dots just below it, and starting to plan a mohawk made of marsh-reed spikes running along the top of the head.

Writing hair spikes...

For ears, I'm adding small spikes plus a simple brass torus ring at the left ear as an earring.

For the shoulders, I'm adding a dome-shaped pauldron with leather coloring and rivet trim scattered around the rim, plus a few bone spikes for extra texture.

Placing fang spikes pointing downward around the neck ring front, then adding a larger tusk pendant hanging in the center with its own spike geometry positioned relative to the neck ring's radius and offset.

Now I'm adding accessories: a leather pouch box on the right hip with a flap and strap, and sketching a bandolier strap draping diagonally across the chest from shoulder to opposite hip, computing path points that hug the torso's surface.

Drape the bandolier strap along a curved path with small outward-pointing bone spikes evenly spaced as decorative teeth, then I'll consider adding a glowing rune decal to the chest.

Skipping extra glow effects on the club or mushrooms to keep complexity down, and for the mud splatter on the legs, I'll just paint it directly using a height-based condition rather than relying on uncertain scatter filtering APIs.

For the moss, I can use the hit normal field to filter upward-facing surfaces. I'm also adding small knee spikes near the leg joints for extra detail, giving toe claws a dark bone color, and now working out arm joint positions for shoulder, elbow, and wrist placement on both sides.

For the hands, I'm placing three small claw spikes with slight x-offsets angled forward-down from each hand, though for the weapon-holding hand I realize the claws would clip through the club handle, so I'm swapping those for knuckle bumps instead to keep the grip looking natural.

Writing the point/vector helpers and skin paint logic...

Still defining panel outlines...

I'm adjusting the panel's lean angle slightly so the bottom doesn't jut out too far, checking it against where the belly bulges at y1.1-1.3 so the belt can sit above and hide the overlap, and now working out how the belt ring's depth needs to clear the belly curve by interpolating the loft between pelvis sections.

Now I'm placing the front and back panels at specific positions, skipping extra side hip details, and moving on to actually write the code referencing the torso sweep.

For the chest decal, I'm designing an SVG war paint texture with three diagonal claw-mark strokes in a pale bone color, planning to skip detailed facial warpaint and maybe just add a simple red strip instead.

For the skull decal, I'm placing a red stripe across the eyes using surface-based positioning with a slight lift to avoid z-fighting with the skull geometry, and checking that it won't collide with brow details. I'm also verifying leg proportions -- capsule radii for thighs and ankles, foot sphere coverage, and hip joint placement -- before finalizing the code with a nullable hit check.
